title: Philip II to Don Juan of Austria, Madrid, 28 Aug 1574 (KHA G016-A0204)

documents.shelfmark: Koninklijk Huisarchief, Collectie Handschriften 2e serie, G016-A0204

plaintext.source: A clear version on a separate sheet in the same item (scans 2 right and 3 left).

transcription.source: clear_version.md (the clear sheet transcribed); cipher read against key.md line by line on ~14 of ~30 lines, not a full sign-level file
transcription.notes: No full sign-level transcription of the cipher.

system.summary: Letters on one- and two-digit numbers near alphabetical order (d 4, l 12, n 14, r 19, s 20, t 21, v 22), vowels a 2/ρ, e 5, i 1, o 6/15, and vowel marks on the preceding sign (cross e, dot i, stroke above u); a few code groups; y written g; numbers in clear.

prior_solution.where: Contemporary clear version on a separate sheet in the same KHA item.

conditions.human_role: Asked to take KHA lead K1 from the Nationaal Archief sweep.

solution.what: Fetched the 6 KHA scans at full size through the Koninklijke Verzamelingen rendition API.
Gachard (Netherlands correspondence, Don Juan from 1576), web search for Esquivia, DECODE dump: no printed or online reading.
Found a clear version of the cipher letter on a separate sheet in the same item (alférez Diego de Esquivia, captive 1558-73).
Aligned the cipher on scan 1 word by word with the clear version and rebuilt the letter table, the vowel marks (cross e, dot i, stroke u) and code groups pe/co/Lo (key.md).
Read ~14 of ~30 cipher lines with the key against the clear version: all agree except hazer/saber at the end of paragraph 1 and the name Oram bey (Hürrem Bey) the decipherer left unclear.

Brice Dudout (Claude Opus 5.5): README read-bar recount of clear_version.md. research/reading_audit/v10_relabel.share gives 433 words and 37 holes (0.921), but the holes are the bracketed abbreviation expansions (r[elaci]on, q[ue], v[uest]ra ...) and the English heading; counting the Spanish body with the expansions as read words gives 406 words and one hole ([?]oran), 0.998 (verify_dudout_20261114.py). The recorded 1.0 holds in substance; v10 --apply would demote the text on the expansions alone. The Koninklijke Verzamelingen rendition API of NOTES.md answers 410 Gone and the scans.json deepzoom paths 404 (14 Nov 2026), so the ~16 cipher lines not compared with the key could not be checked.

Project check of PR #570 (Brice Dudout): his recount re-run on clear_version.md: 406 words, one hole ([?]oran), 0.998; v10_relabel.share gives 433 words and 37 holes because it counts the bracketed abbreviation expansions as holes. read_share set to 0.998 (was 1.0); class unchanged. The Koninklijke Verzamelingen rendition address answers 410 Gone (checked 14 Nov 2026).

outcome.method_basis: The item carries a clear version of the cipher on a separate sheet; the key was rebuilt from that pair and confirms it on the lines checked.

texts.transcription_missing: The cipher passages were read from the separate clear version of the time (clear_version.md, shown under Decryption), checked against the cipher with the key; they were not transcribed sign by sign.
texts.summary: Philip II recommends the alférez Diego de Esquivia, a former captive of Hasan Pasha, to serve near Don Juan at 15 escudos a month, and sends through him answers to Hürrem Bey, the Sultan's chief interpreter, and to Mostafa, a Milanese renegade engineer with Uluç Ali's fleet, both encouraged to keep serving Spain.

reading_review.note: The clear version reads as continuous Spanish; checked against the cipher with the rebuilt key on ~14 lines. Not checked by a person.

outcome.notes: Read from the clear sheet in the same item; key rebuilt and checked on sampled lines.
